records.current_summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): south-east; conservative. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey. Dossier finding: no sub-national divergence documented for this province — it is among the 73 units left at the national score (no province-specific ordinance, incident series or different legal system found). The dossier's only regional-grade note for the south-east is security practice (emergency-era policing, high police presence, village-guard system) rather than law. National context for its sources: a leaked omnibus package (the "11th Judicial Package", Oct 2025) would criminalise LGBT identity and advocacy (up to 3 years; same-sex ceremonies up to 4 years) and raise gender-affirming-care eligibility to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate; the 2025 national monitoring report records hostility institutionalised as state policy.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): the leaked '11th Judicial Package' omnibus reform would amend the penal code to criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy (up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', up to 4 years for same-sex ceremonies) and the civil code to raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. National context for this province.

Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 (24 Feb 2026), 'A Major Siege': in 2025 hostility became explicit state policy (presidency-centred, with the family ministry implementing); documents 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings, trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51), and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5x the prior year), based on media cases because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics. National context for this province.

sources.claim: Human Rights news release (29 October 2025): the leaked 11th Judicial Package omnibus draft law would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality" (up to three years), sharply restrict gender-affirming healthcare (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility conditions) and allow criminal charges against both trans people and the professionals providing their care; the government's stated justification is protecting "the family" and "public morals"; the package also carries unrelated measures such as longer child sentences and online-content removal.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People" (published 24 February 2026): finds that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy — centred on the presidency, with the family ministry as the implementing ministry, religious and broadcasting authorities deployed against LGBTI+ people, and the closure of an LGBTI+ rights organisation within this structure.
